text:
jules: FYI a customer hit a nasty one running notebooks + FastAPI: our AsyncClient spawns a loop incorrectly and they saw TLS hangs + warnings about 'There is no current event loop'.

jules: Repro they gave (very small):

```
import asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient

client = AsyncClient()  # from inside a notebook cell or under uvicorn
await client.embedding("hello")
```

jules: In notebooks this sometimes results in `DeprecationWarning: There is no current event loop` or `RuntimeError: Cannot run the event loop while another loop is running`.

irene: sounds like our init tries `asyncio.get_event_loop()` and falls back to `asyncio.run(...)` if not set. Both are fragile: get_event_loop can return a loop tied to the wrong thread in py3.10+, and asyncio.run is never ok from inside an existing loop.

rob: quick background: libraries should not call asyncio.run or rely on global loop policy. Two safe patterns:
- If inside a running loop (get_running_loop succeeds) -> schedule a task with create_task
- If no loop -> start a new loop in a dedicated thread and run tasks there

pat: RFC idea: expose two constructors
- AsyncClient.from_sync() -> intended for sync apps, will create a thread loop for background refresh
- AsyncClient() -> assume caller will await; do not start threads/run loop implicitly

jules: I like that. It makes behavior explicit and reduces surprises for frameworks. Docs + deprecation path for old behavior.

irene: implementation notes: if we spawn a thread loop, create a new loop via asyncio.new_event_loop(), set it on the thread only (loop.run_forever), and use asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe to schedule refresh. Avoid calling `asyncio.set_event_loop` on main thread.

rob: watch out for httpx AsyncClient: it binds sockets to whatever loop is running during connection creation. If we create httpx clients on main thread but then use them from a different loop/thread we can get stuck TLS handshakes. Solution: create httpx.AsyncClient lazily inside the loop used to send requests or ensure transport/socket lifecycle stays on one loop.

pat: test plan:
- add pytest-asyncio test that instantiates AsyncClient inside running loop and asserts no exception
- add threaded integration test where sync constructor creates thread-loop, call generate concurrently from main thread with run_coroutine_threadsafe
- add notebook smoke test in CI matrix (use nbclient or run via ipykernel) to catch the common case

jules: can we add a short troubleshooting section to the README: "Using AsyncClient in frameworks & notebooks" with dos/don'ts and migrations? saves support noise.

irene: yes. Also add a note about uvloop: discouraging changing loop policy while our client is bootstrapping. That change can move transports under different loop impl and cause odd races.

infra-bot: Created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/1509 "AsyncClient: avoid asyncio.run/get_event_loop in library init; add sync/async constructors and tests" assigned to @pat P1

pat: I'll open a PR with the constructors + tests + docs. Will ping infra for the notebook CI job.

jules: great — I'll attach the user's minimal repro to the issue. Thanks all.
